content:
Rafael Mendes: Dropping the draft Dedicated throughput SLO escalation runbook here for feedback. Pls review esp: paging thresholds, comms, and what "SLO miss" means in practice. https://confluence.redwood.dev/eng-sre/runbooks/dedicated-throughput-slo-escalation (WIP)

Sean Gallagher: skimmed. main gap: we need to be super explicit about the *signal* used to declare a miss. Right now it's half metric / half symptom-based.
Sean Gallagher: Suggest section 0: "Definition" w/ canonical metric + window. e.g. `dedicated_throughput_floor_compliance` over 30m rolling, exclude minutes with customer-side throttling.

Aisha Bello: +1. Also the runbook references "Throughput SLO Dashboard" but no link / panel names. Can we add the exact dashboard UID + the 3 panels we expect oncall to look at first?
Aisha Bello: Proposed: 1) Floor compliance over time (per deployment_id), 2) Saturation signals (queue depth / GPU util / KV cache hit), 3) Admission control shed rate (tier-aware) so we know if we’re protecting floors by shedding.

Sergio Costa: I can paste the dashboard link once the panels PR merges (observability-pack#842). For now: https://grafana.redwood.dev/d/dedicated-slo/dedicated-throughput-slo (internal)
Sergio Costa: Panel naming is in flux tho. If you want stable names, we should align in the doc.

Allison Grant: Please do align. We got burned on "SLO" dashboards drifting from runbooks. Recommend we reference by tag/annotation (dashboard has `runbook:dedicated-throughput`) and list panel IDs.

Dev Patel: From Support/CS POV: we need a clear "when do we tell the customer" trigger.
Dev Patel: Runbook currently says "notify CS for customer-impacting" but that’s subjective. Can we define it like: if burn rate alert fires OR sustained below floor > 15m = page oncall + notify #customer-success-oncall?

Rachel Kim: yes please. Also include comms template. Even 3 bullets:
Rachel Kim: - acknowledge + what we’re checking
Rachel Kim: - expected next update time (30m?)
Rachel Kim: - workaround ask (can they reduce concurrency / pin model version / switch region if Premium)

Rafael Mendes: makes sense. For triggers: we already have two burn-rate alerts in the draft (fast + slow). I can add "if fast burn fires, customer-impacting by default unless proven customer-caused".

Irene Choi: infra notes: runbook needs a step for "is this actually a capacity deficit vs routing".
Irene Choi: We’ve seen cases where deployment got mapped to wrong pool during partial rollout. Step should check tier->pool selector logs + feature flag state.

Mina Haddad: yep. Add:
Mina Haddad: 1) check `routing_policy_version` tag on metrics
Mina Haddad: 2) confirm deployment is pinned to expected pool/shape
Mina Haddad: 3) if mismatch: rollback flag to previous selector + re-route

Vanessa Ortiz: Also add "warm pool" expectations per tier.
Vanessa Ortiz: For Premium we maintain spare capacity; for Standard not guaranteed. Oncall needs to know if "scale up" is an option vs "manage load".

Owen Phillips: Another real gap: how to handle streaming token accounting. We had double counting recently (PR-19422). Runbook should say: if customer reports mismatch between their calc and our dashboard, check metric version + streaming accounted tokens.
Owen Phillips: maybe a small "Common pitfalls" section.

Sean Gallagher: Agree. Also exclusions:
Sean Gallagher: - customer request rate > contracted (burst) not a miss
Sean Gallagher: - unsupported model/version (customer changed without notifying) not a miss
Sean Gallagher: - customer-side throttling / 4xx due to quota not a miss
Sean Gallagher: But we need clear evidence requirements so we don’t hand-wave.

Aisha Bello: For evidence: add a screenshot checklist: dashboard snapshot + query links.
Aisha Bello: Also: runbook says "check deploy health" but doesn't specify. I'd add the standard triage: error rate, p50/p95 latency, queue, GPU util, node restarts.

Rafael Mendes: ok. I'll add a "Triage checklist" w/ direct queries.
Rafael Mendes: For burn-rate thresholds, are we good with 2%/1h and 5%/6h style? (mirroring latency SLO practice)

Sean Gallagher: I think so, but we should note that throughput can be noisy w/ batching/caching changes. Maybe require 2 consecutive evaluations before paging?

Allison Grant: careful: adding debounce at evaluator vs alert rule changes semantics. If we want that, document it.
Allison Grant: I'd rather keep alert rules standard and add "confirm w/ dashboard" step before declaring incident.

Connor O'Brien: release angle: runbook should specify when to page infra vs handle via config.
Connor O'Brien: Ex: if we can adjust admission control caps or move to adjacent pool, do that before paging fleet/procurement.

Dev Patel: Also need credit/comp hook. Not asking to decide policy here, but at least "if confirmed Redwood-cause miss > X minutes, open INT ticket + tag Finance".

Rachel Kim: +1. At minimum: who approves credits and what artifacts are needed.

Rafael Mendes: I'll add a final section:
Rafael Mendes: - "Customer comms + cadence"
Rafael Mendes: - "Credit evaluation handoff" (links to policy doc once Legal final)
Rafael Mendes: - "Post-incident": file retro + update runbook + capture capacity action items

Sergio Costa: Re dashboards: I can lock names this week. If you list panels as "Floor compliance (by deployment_id)" etc I’ll match.

Irene Choi: please add explicit owner contacts for escalation. like "Page SRE" vs "@fleet-ops".

Rafael Mendes: noted. Will update and repost in-thread for final skim tomorrow.

Aisha Bello: one more: can we add "what to ask the customer" checklist?
Aisha Bello: - model + version
Aisha Bello: - region
Aisha Bello: - max context, streaming yes/no
Aisha Bello: - concurrency / req rate
Aisha Bello: It helps a lot in the first 10m.

Rafael Mendes: yes. Adding.

Sean Gallagher: thanks. Once updated, I’ll sign off as SLO owner. We should make sure this runbook is linked from the burn-rate alert annotations.

Allison Grant: +1. Add runbook URL in alert rule labels (`runbook_url`).

Rafael Mendes: done (will go in PR w/ alert rule updates).
